attempted_claim: Fix integer k>=3 and let L=l0(x)+l1(x)Phi_k+l2(x)Phi_k^2 with li in C[x], l0*l2 nonzero and coprime, Phi_k(f)(x)=f(x^k), acting on formal Puiseux series. Assume the Newton polygon of L at 0 has two distinct finite slopes. Prove or disprove the dichotomy: if L has no order-one right factor over C(x^{1/*}) (equivalently the associated Mahler-Riccati equation has no rational solution) then the difference Galois group of L over C(x) contains SL_2(C) and every nonzero Puiseux solution of L(f)=0 is differentially transcendental over C(x) (satisfies no nonzero algebraic differential equation over C(x)). A complete answer proves this implication for all such L or gives one explicit counterexample L0 with distinct slopes, certified irreducible, plus a nonzero Puiseux solution and a nonzero differential polynomial over C(x) it satisfies.
claim_type: universal dichotomy: SL2 Galois plus full hypertranscendence
decisive_failure: The Galois-inclusion and parametrized hypertranscendence criteria could not be sourced because the single literature call failed at the tool layer, and the counterexample search found no differentially algebraic solution (L0 has no power-series solution to order 30).
